editorial_index_description: Learn how to read the map, weather, earthquake, species, cuisine and destination data, with sources and limitations.
editorial_index_body:
These guides explain what each map layer shows, where its data comes from and what a missing or dated record means. They are references for exploring the atlas, not official alerts or a guarantee of completeness.

Start with the region guide to understand what a province selection means. Use the conditions guide before interpreting a weather or disaster layer, and the species and destinations guide before reusing photos, recipes or records. Each guide includes a concrete reading example and links to the underlying data documentation.
editorial_about_description: Explore Indonesia's regions, landscapes, weather, wildlife, food and places on a source-aware interactive map.
editorial_about_body:
Atlas Nusantara is a map-based way to explore Indonesia. It brings together administrative regions, landscapes, public environmental information, wildlife, cuisine and tourist destinations. Select a province or city to see what the available datasets say about it.

## Key features

The interactive map combines a searchable directory of 38 provinces and 514 cities and regencies with source-derived coastlines and relief. Layers include dated weather and earthquakes, mountains, flora, fauna, cuisine, destinations and selected disaster reports. Some views support search, filtering, downloads and links back to their source.

## How it works

The administrative directory follows a pinned 2025 Kemendagri transcription. Its geometry comes from an older 2020 BPS/OCHA dataset matched to the newer region codes. Terrain is modelled using NOAA ETOPO1. Weather forecasts come from representative BMKG village points, not a measurement at every spot on the map. Dataset coverage, dates, usage terms and attribution differ by layer. See [source and edition notes](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/blob/main/docs/DATA_SOURCES.md).

## Important limitations

Boundaries are simplified and not a legal, cadastral or navigational reference. Cloud movement, wind visualization and sea effects are illustrative, not measured conditions. Source records may be incomplete, outdated, approximate or preliminary. Missing results do not mean zero risk. **Atlas Nusantara is not an emergency alert service.** Follow official warnings from BMKG and BNPB.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the weather information live?

No. Weather and earthquake records are dated snapshots. Check the source and retrieval time shown in the layer before using a value.

### Why is a place or photo missing?

Coverage varies across providers. An unavailable photo may reflect incomplete attribution or licensing, not the absence of the destination, dish or species.

### Can I use this map as an official boundary or safety reference?

No. Use authoritative government maps and official emergency channels for legal boundaries, warnings and safety decisions.

## Who maintains this atlas

Atlas Nusantara is an independent project from [Readynaz](https://readynaz.com), not an official publication or alert system of BMKG, BNPB or any other data provider. The atlas adds its own navigation, visualizations and joins between source datasets; the underlying records belong to their respective publishers. Original source dates and dataset limitations matter more than how polished a map looks. If you notice a mismatched location, missing attribution or an outdated description, report the specific record and its source in the [project repository](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/issues).
editorial_regions_description: Understand the 2025 region directory, older geometry, relief and how map selection works.
editorial_regions_body:
## Administrative codes and editions

The directory lists 38 provinces, 416 regencies and 98 cities. Its codes follow a pinned 2025 transcription from [cahyadsn/wilayah](https://github.com/cahyadsn/wilayah). This is a versioned directory, not a claim that every border was newly surveyed in 2025. Region names and codes can change between editions.

## Why the boundaries have a different date

The outlines use BPS/OCHA COD-AB data valid in 2020, mapped to the newer administrative directory with an explicit crosswalk. BPS and Kemendagri identifiers are not interchangeable. The mapping matches known units but does not certify every 2025 boundary change. Small islands and coastlines are simplified.

## How to explore a region

Choose a province on the map, search the directory, or use the region table. Selecting a regency or city moves the camera to its area; it does not change the underlying projection. The altitude and seabed shading use NOAA ETOPO1 and are vertically exaggerated for visibility.

## Reading the map responsibly

Treat geometry as a discovery tool, not a survey, legal boundary or marine navigation chart. If a location looks displaced, check the source edition and the point coordinates before drawing conclusions. Read the [geometry documentation](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/blob/main/docs/GEOMETRY.md) and [data-source notes](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/blob/main/docs/DATA_SOURCES.md).

## Example: a province and its boundary are not the same dataset

Open the atlas and select Aceh using the region list or map. Its administrative code and name come from the pinned 2025 directory, while the displayed outline was derived from a different dataset with a 2020 reference date. Those two facts can both be correct. The map uses a documented crosswalk to bring them together, but does not establish that the visible boundary is legally current. To check an address, title of land or disputed boundary, use the appropriate government source rather than the visual outline.
editorial_conditions_description: Interpret dated BMKG snapshots and mixed disaster reports without mistaking them for live alerts.
editorial_conditions_body:
## Weather snapshots

The weather layer uses captured BMKG forecasts for representative village points in Indonesia's cities and regencies. A point is not a complete observation of its surrounding area. Always check source and retrieval timestamps. Interpolated wind, clouds and waves are visual aids, not measured marine or satellite data.

## Earthquakes and warnings

Earthquake observations are dated records, not predictions or a list of every tremor. Some warning feeds are subject to approval and publication checks. If no warning appears, the atlas cannot tell you that conditions are safe.

## Disaster reports need context

Official BNPB records, citizen submissions on PetaBencana and geocoded news headlines can have different standards of verification and location accuracy. A report can be preliminary, duplicated, imprecise or delayed. Hazard polygons from InaRISK are not connected. Do not combine report counts as if they were a complete national incident total.

## What to do with a serious warning

Use the original provider and its timestamp, and consult [BMKG](https://www.bmkg.go.id/) and [BNPB](https://www.bnpb.go.id/) for current official advice. The atlas is for exploration and context, **not emergency notification**. See [source limitations](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/blob/main/docs/DATA_SOURCES.md).

## Example: reading a forecast without overstating it

Open the Weather layer and choose a province, then a city or regency. First identify which representative village the forecast refers to and when the data was issued or retrieved. Next distinguish the provider's numbers from the animated clouds, wind and sea, which are illustrative. If you switch to the Earthquakes layer, compare the occurrence time and source of each observation rather than treating a plotted point as a prediction. An empty layer, stale timestamp or missing warning is never an all-clear; use the current [BMKG](https://www.bmkg.go.id/) and [BNPB](https://www.bnpb.go.id/) channels for safety decisions.
editorial_nature_description: Explore biodiversity, traditional food and tourism records while respecting coverage and attribution.
editorial_nature_body:
## Flora and fauna

Species names and records come from a mixture of GBIF-derived checklists, conservation sources including KSDAE, and iNaturalist. A species shown in a province means it has source-linked evidence there; it does not count all individuals or prove the species is absent elsewhere. IUCN status and Indonesian legal protection are different fields. Images retain credits and licence information.

## Indonesian cuisine

The cuisine layer groups dishes by province using source associations, including the Indonesian Wikipedia list. That is not proof of a dish's exclusive origin. Recipe availability differs by dish and language; source links lead to Cookpad, a licensed recipe dataset or reviewed examples. Follow the linked recipe for exact ingredients and preparation rather than treating a summary as instructions.

## Destinations and photographs

Destination records are drawn from publicly accessible SISPARNAS data and organized into province collections. They are not a complete list of every tourist attraction. A missing category, coordinate or photo is not evidence that a destination does not exist. Images are used subject to available permissions and attribution.

## Check before reusing

Follow each item's source link, date and image credit. Look at [species methodology](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/blob/main/docs/SPECIES.md), [cuisine sources](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/blob/main/docs/CUISINE.md) and [destination coverage](https://github.com/ygrip/atlas-nusantara/blob/main/docs/DESTINATIONS.md) before reproducing records.

## Example: compare three kinds of evidence

Select a province and open a species record. Its occurrence evidence, IUCN category and Indonesian legal-protection status answer different questions; read them separately. In the Cuisine layer, a dish linked to that province means the source associated it with the place, not that the province exclusively invented it. Follow the original recipe link for ingredients and instructions. In Destinations, use the original record and photo credit before sharing a claim or reusing an image. The atlas joins these sources for exploration; it does not independently verify every record.
privacy_ads_disclosure: Google advertising may be requested on the English-language homepage. Google can receive device and network data and may use cookies or similar storage. privacy_turnstile_disclosure: When you request a downloadable archive, Cloudflare Turnstile may check browser and network signals to reduce automated abuse. Ordinary map browsing does not need this verification. See [Cloudflare's privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/).
privacy_counter_disclosure: Download rate-limit counters store a hashed network address in D1, rather than the original address. The counters expire after their window and are deleted by scheduled cleanup, which may be delayed. They are used for security, not analytics.
terms_ads_disclosure: The English-language homepage may request one clearly labelled Google advertisement. Ads are separate from the atlas, data sources and public-safety guidance, and do not imply endorsement. Blocked, empty or failed ads do not limit browsing. Display depends on publisher approval, availability and applicable consent requirements.
terms_download_disclosure: Archive downloads use Cloudflare Turnstile and request, size and daily limits. Passing verification does not allow access to an unavailable dataset. Do not bypass safeguards or treat the atlas as an emergency-alert service.
language_source_note: A language spoken in several provinces is counted in each of them. The source predates the 2022 Papua split; languages of Papua and Papua Barat are placed in the 2025 provinces from the districts named in their descriptions.
